recipes.name: Cranberry and Almond Rice Pilaf
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt, or to taste

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook and stir onions in hot oil until tender and translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in rice and cranberries until rice is coated with oil and lightly toasted, about 5 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth; season with kosher salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 22 minutes.
Remove the skillet from heat; stir in green onions, almonds, and cilantro. Adjust seasoning if needed.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry and Almond Rice Pilaf
raw_recipe.description: This cranberry rice pilaf features sweet-tart dried cranberries, onion, cilantro, and crunchy slivered almonds for a delicious, hearty side dish.

review.reviewBody: Wow! This was delicious. Been trying to find a recipe similar to Fish City Grill's rice that they serve with their talapia. This wasn't it, but it was absolutely delicious, and I'm glad I tried it. It has a mildly sweet flavor that complements my blackened talapia toning down some of the spiciness. Easy to make too. It was great without the cilantro and extra onions, but I might try them next time just to see the difference. The slivered almonds are a must though.

I really like the basics of this recipe, but we are a family that hates cilantro. Subbed it with fresh parsley, and this was a big hit. Also, I toasted the almonds before adding them to the mix. Yum! Served this with salmon and asparagus, made a beautiful plate.

9.21.21 I accidentally used basmati rice instead of jasmine (and I even had it in the pantry), but I think it cooked up fine in spite of that. We eat a lot of rice, and I’m so glad I found a new recipe to incorporate into our menus. The only thing that I did differently was to toast the almonds which enhances the flavor of the nuts and gives them just a little crunch. No other changes made with this recipe, it’s just about perfect in my opinion.

This was excellent! I will definitely make it again at Christmas. I'm generally not a fan of fruit cooked or mixed with "regular" food, but I really liked this. I toasted the almonds and would recommend that extra step.

This rice was a huge success.
I did not have the chicken broth on hand, so I found a package of dry chicken noodle soup and used the whole package as it called for 4 c of water. I reduced the amount a fraction.
I used regular rice, I had on hand.
Great recipe. Recommendation came as using for Christmas or Thanksgiving dish.

OH-EMMM-GEEEEE! This dish was so yummy. I used a little less broth (ran out) and added a 1/2 teaspoon of minced garlic. My husband, kids and neighbor he dropped in loved it. I served it with Apricot/Raisin Glazed Salmon and fresh broccoli. What an easy and delicious meal over-all. It's official.....I'm a GOURMET COOK!
Awesome, skipped green onions everything else followed recipe, used homemade beef broth was so good!

Excellent recipe! It is easy and tastes awesome! I really like the flavor that the cranberries add to the pilaf. I did not have jasmine rice. I used the generic long grain rice I had on hand and it turned out great. I will definitely make this again.

This was exactly what I was looking for...super easy and delicious. I didn't have jasmine, so I used brown rice instead, and it came out wonderfully. Perfect side for some chicken or fish. Will definitely be making this more often.
Made exactly as instructed and it was ok, not great. It's missing something for taste.
I make this weekly! My kids are obsessed and it’s so easy to make! Only adjustment is we leave out the cilantro.
We have been using this recipe for years and especially love it as a side dish for our grilled salmon. Easy and always gets rave reviews!

I have made this several times now. It’s great. The mixture of cranberries and almonds adds sweetness and nuttiness that blends well with rice. I used basmati rice rather than jasmine rice. The texture is a little different but more similar to pilaf I’ve had in the past. The grains remain separate rather than clumping together.My family of three always has leftovers, but it never lasts long.

Wow! Rice doesn’t have to be so boring! This is delish and I eat the leftovers for lunch the next day all by itself ! The combo of green onion and cilantro with the cranberries is a match made in heaven. And it looks great too! Presentation is important to me especially when your serving to guests and it always gets rave reviews . I must give the almonds credit also not just for the great added taste but a little crunchy Never hurt . I often have all the ingredients in my pantry. I made it as it is written several times and once with cran- cherries and wow! A little more sweet is always welcome at my Table .allrecpies is my “go-to” and this side dish is the best one I’ve ever made.
Will make this one over and over again!

Made this for my husband and I and we can't eat enough of it. Has become our favorite side dish. Did not alter the recipe in any way. I did use my homemade chicken broth for a slightly healthier touch.
This was so good, and a nice change of pace to go with chicken
